titles.incident: What to do in an incident
titles.competitions: FIS, Freeride World Tour & other events

PortalContent.c2: A concise guide to the FIS rules. Read the official document for the complete wording.
PortalContent.c4: Do not put others in danger.
PortalContent.c6: Match your speed to your ability, visibility, snow and traffic.
PortalContent.c8: Protect people ahead when approaching from behind.
PortalContent.c10: Give others ample space when passing.
PortalContent.c12: Look uphill and downhill before joining or restarting.
PortalContent.c14: Avoid narrow or hidden stopping places; clear them after a fall.
PortalContent.c16: Use the piste edge when walking.
PortalContent.c22: Those involved and witnesses exchange contact details.
PortalContent.c24: Use the resort’s current map and signs to confirm the difficulty of each piste. Colors indicate difficulty, not whether a piste is open.
PortalContent.c28: Easier marked pistes; remain in control.
PortalContent.c30: More demanding terrain for confident skiers.
PortalContent.c34: Patrol helps with mountain safety and incident response. Verified local patrol phone numbers are not yet available in this directory.
PortalContent.c35: Follow posted closures and local patrol instructions. Resort-specific freeride rules and current avalanche bulletins must be checked before entering off-piste terrain.
PortalContent.c37: In an emergency, contact 112 and follow the operator’s instructions.
PortalContent.c39: Request emergency help when it is needed.
PortalContent.c41: Give your exact location, what happened and your name.
PortalContent.c43: Speak clearly and do not end the call until the operator finishes.
PortalContent.c46: Emergency assistance throughout Georgia, 24 hours a day.
